Real Estate for the Cost of Unpaid Taxes in Seminole County

What if a property worth hundreds of thousands of dollars was sitting there, waiting for you — just for the cost of unpaid taxes? That’s exactly what’s happening in Seminole County’s tax sales.

If you’ve ever thought about investing, this could be your chance.

Seminole County, Florida Tax Sales: A Complete Guide

Are you thinking about buying property through tax sales in Seminole County? Here’s everything you need to know, explained in a simple way.

Important Details: Seminole County Tax Deed Sales

Quick Look at Seminole County Tax Certificate Sales

How the Process Works

Tax Certificate Sale
Each May, Seminole County holds an online auction at LienHub. Investors bid by offering the lowest interest rate they’re willing to accept. The lower your offer, the better your chances of winning.

Redeem or Deed Application
Owners have 2 years to pay back the taxes. If they don’t, the certificate holder can start a tax deed application.

Tax Deed Auction
Once a deed application is ready, the property is sold at a public auction through the Seminole Clerk’s Office. The winner gets a tax deed — but you might need a court action later to clear the title.

Key Tips for Bidding at Seminole County Tax Deed Sales

  • Research every property. Always check ownership, liens, and physical condition.
  • Bring the right payment. After winning, you must pay a deposit immediately. The rest is due the next day.
  • Understand title risks. Tax deeds might not give you a clean title. Sometimes you need legal help to fix it.
  • No refunds, no inspections. Sales are final. Properties are sold “as-is.”

Fun Facts About Real Estate in Seminole County

  • One of Central Florida’s Fastest-Growing Markets
    Homes sell quickly thanks to great schools and family-friendly neighborhoods.
  • Top-Rated Schools
    Cities like Lake Mary, Oviedo, and Winter Springs are known for excellent education, boosting home prices.
  • Outdoor Lifestyle
    Tons of parks, trails, lakes, and river access make this a top choice for outdoor lovers.
  • Strong Job Market
    Healthcare, tech, and education sectors drive steady job growth, helping keep housing demand high.
  • New Communities are Growing
    Places like Sanford and Oviedo are seeing lots of new construction with modern, master-planned communities.

Why Seminole County is a Great Spot for Tax Deed Investing

  • High demand for real estate from families and professionals
  • Great returns with tax certificates earning up to 18% interest
  • Properties often sell for less than market value
  • Online auctions make it easy to participate, even from out-of-state
  • Open to local and international investors

FAQs About Seminole County Tax Deed Sales

Q: Do I need to be a Florida resident to buy?
A: No, anyone can participate, including out-of-state and international investors.

Q: Can I inspect the property before bidding?
A: No official inspections are allowed. You can drive by, but buyers purchase “as-is.”

Q: What happens if I don’t pay the full amount after winning?
A: You lose your deposit, and the property goes back to auction.

Q: Is the title clean after buying a tax deed?
A: Not always. You may need a quiet title lawsuit to clear any ownership issues.

Q: Where can I find properties coming up for auction?
A: You can view listings on the Seminole County Tax Deed Auction Site or on the Seminole Clerk’s Auction Calendar.

Pro Tips

  • Always conduct a title search before bidding.
  • Plan your budget carefully, including any necessary legal costs.
  • Be ready to pay quickly after the auction.
  • Please note: No refunds, no inspections, and no guarantees.
